title: Exploration of the regulatory mechanism of PD-L1 expression in pMMR AGS gastric cancer cell by cytotoxic drugs and anti-angiogenic drugs
task: Determine PD-L1 regulatory mechanisms downstream of cytotoxic and anti-angiogenic drugs in pMMR gastric cancer
key_results: 5-FU (64 µM), cisplatin (16 µM), and apatinib (320 nM) significantly upregulated PD-L1 mRNA and protein; all drugs increased PI3K expression with divergent effects on downstream effectors (apatinib increased Akt phosphorylation; 5-FU upregulated MEK1/ERK)
comments: The divergent pathway effects across drugs suggest multiple regulatory nodes for PD-L1 induction rather than a single linear pathway, complicating therapeutic predictions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cytotoxic and anti-angiogenic drugs upregulate PD-L1 via PI3K/Akt/mTOR and MAPK pathways in pMMR gastric cancer
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for PD-L1 upregulation; pathway involvement heterogeneous across drugs

title: Amyloid and aging reshape glial waste management in APP/PS1 mice
task: Characterize age- and amyloid-dependent remodeling of glial waste-handling structures in Alzheimer's disease models
key_results: PAS+ polyglucosan granules increased markedly with age and amyloid pathology; extraparenchymal IgM+ granules declined with age; IgM+ astrocytes increased robustly with aging and were more abundant in APP/PS1 mice, co-expressing complement C3
comments: The shift from extraparenchymal to intracellular/complement-mediated waste handling is intriguing but correlative; causality and functional consequences remain unclear.

model_io.model: APPswe/PS1dE9 transgenic mice and C57BL/6 controls

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aging and amyloid pathology remodel glial waste-handling architecture, shifting from early extraparenchymal structures to late-life intracellular sequestration and complement-mediated responses
hypotheses.result: Confirmed through age-dependent and genotype-dependent distribution changes

title: Specific targeting of cancer cell mitochondria with a malaria drug improves pancreatic cancer outcome
task: Develop mitochondria-targeted artemisinin conjugate for enhanced pancreatic cancer therapy with diagnostic imaging
key_results: DZ-ART1 accumulated 5-10 fold more in cancer vs. normal cells; significantly decreased survival of 8 PDAC lines; prolonged survival and suppressed tumor growth/metastasis in KPC transgenic, syngeneic, and PDX models without normal tissue toxicity
comments: The mitochondria-dependence is elegantly validated by loss of uptake upon mitochondrial depletion, though translational efficacy in human trials remains unproven.

model_io.model: KPC transgenic, syngeneic, and PDX mouse models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tumor-targeted artemisinin conjugate selectively disrupts cancer cell mitochondria to enhance anti-tumor efficacy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; mitochondrial depletion blocked DZ-ART1 uptake and cytotoxicity

key_results: 93.29% and 96.75% accuracy on Full Transcript and Mature mRNA datasets; 5.31% and 3.37% improvement over existing methods
comments: The hybrid feature representation and SHAP-based selection are sound, but cross-validation and test sets are not fully independent in benchmarking contexts.

title: A network toxicology and machine learning approach to uncover the molecular machinery of bisphenol A-induced colorectal cancer
task: Uncover molecular networks linking bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to colorectal cancer
key_results: Identified 12-gene CRC signature overlapping BPA targets (MET, SORD, DPEP1, KIT, RIPK2, SET, HSP90AB1, DBF4, MMP1, MMP12, ANPEP, GLA); stable BPA–protein binding predicted by docking
comments: Integration of network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking is comprehensive, but the 12-gene signature requires experimental validation to confirm causality.

outputs: predicted binding interactions and stability scores

hypotheses.hypothesis: BPA targets a conserved set of genes dysregulated in colorectal cancer

title: Three novel actinomycetes, Nocardia spongicola sp. nov., Pseudonocardia oceanicola sp. nov. and Streptomyces callyspongiae sp. nov., isolated from marine sponges
task: Taxonomic characterization and description of three novel actinomycete species from marine sponges
key_results: Three novel species proposed: Nocardia spongicola, Pseudonocardia oceanicola, and Streptomyces callyspongiae; secondary metabolite extracts showed cytotoxic activity against H460 lung cancer cells with apoptotic induction
comments: Polyphasic taxonomy approach is rigorous; genome mining identifies biosynthetic potential, but link between secondary metabolite production and isolate identity needs clarification.

model_io.model: 16S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenomic analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Marine sponge-derived actinomycetes possess novel secondary metabolite biosynthetic capacity
hypotheses.result: Multiple biosynthetic gene clusters identified; extracts from two strains induce apoptosis in lung cancer cells

title: A comparative study of HSO-optimized PID and TID controllers with fuzzy adaptation for delta robot control
task: Control highly nonlinear Delta robot using Harmony-Search-optimized and fuzzy-adaptive PID/TID controllers
key_results: Fuzzy TID achieves lowest RMSE on sinusoidal tracking (0.2602 mm X, 0.3046 mm Y, 0.6548 mm Z) and stair inputs; optimized TID reduces steady-state error (0.2982 vs. 2.2705 for θ₁)
comments: Comprehensive experimental validation with identified NLARX model (MSE 0.02662); fuzzy TID superior on accuracy but optimized TID offers lower complexity for real-time implementation.

title: Modeling of fault-resilient digital circuits with perceptrons

title: A simulation study on the effect of bifurcation angles on the temperature characteristics in bifurcated tunnel fires
task: Predict maximum gas temperature and decay in bifurcated tunnel fires
key_results: Empirical model ΔTmax/T0 = (5.855 + 1.921sinθ) Q*2/3 established; temperature decay follows double-exponential model with geometry-dependent parameters
comments: High-fidelity FDS simulations provide practical tools for fire-safety design but validation against real tunnel fires would strengthen claims.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Classic dimensionless relationship ΔTmax/T0 ∝ kQ*2/3 remains valid with geometry-dependent constant k
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; k strongly depends on bifurcation angle θ
